title: VingCard Compatible RFID Hotel Key Cards — Ultralight AES Upgrade Matrix
summary: ProudTek RFID cards are fully compatible with VingCard hotel locks across the Essence, Allure and Classic series using MIFARE Classic 1K, MIFARE Ultralight C and the newly announced MIFARE Ultralight AES credentials. VingCard, part of ASSA ABLOY Global Solutions and the world's most widely installed hotel lock system, has recently adopted MIFARE Ultralight AES as its next-generation credential standard, offering enhanced security with a smaller memory footprint and lower per-card manufacturing cost. The compatibility matrix on this page maps every current VingCard lock series to its supported chip families, mobile access capabilities and VISIONLINE software integration. Properties running VISIONLINE access management can specify MIFARE Ultralight AES for future-proof deployments, while legacy estates continue to use MIFARE Classic 1K and Ultralight C with full firmware support. The Essence and Allure series additionally support mobile access through ASSA ABLOY Mobile Access SDK for seamless phone-based room entry. Each chip-lock combination listed below has been verified through ProudTek bench testing using VingCard reference encoders and VISIONLINE integration workflows. Request a free test-card kit to validate compatibility with your specific VingCard lock hardware and software platform before committing to production volumes.

sections.intro: All VingCard locks accept ISO/IEC 14443A credentials, but supported chip families vary by hardware generation and VISIONLINE software version. MIFARE Ultralight AES represents VingCard's strategic pivot toward smaller, more secure credentials.

callout.label: Ultralight AES cost advantage
callout.text: MIFARE Ultralight AES represents the future of VingCard credentials. With only 888 bytes of usable memory versus 1,024 for Classic, AES enables smaller, cheaper cards with better security. Properties can upgrade from Classic 1K to Ultralight AES without lock firmware changes, achieving per-card cost savings of 8-12% while improving encryption.

sections.title: The VingCard Migration Path: From Classic to Ultralight AES
sections.intro: VingCard is actively transitioning properties away from MIFARE Classic 1K toward Ultralight C and the new Ultralight AES standard. This shift addresses cost, memory efficiency and security concerns while maintaining backward compatibility.

sections.title: VingCard Compatibility Verification and Encoding Workflow
sections.intro: ProudTek follows a five-stage process that validates Ultralight AES, Ultralight C and Classic 1K credentials against the property's VISIONLINE version and lock hardware before bulk production begins.

items.label: Stage 1 — Lock estate audit
items.text: Property provides VingCard lock model numbers, firmware versions and current VISIONLINE software version deployed in the access-management system.

items.label: Stage 2 — Credential path selection
items.text: ProudTek assesses the property's timeline and security requirements, recommending Ultralight AES for new deployments, Ultralight C for cost optimization, or Classic 1K for legacy compatibility.

items.label: Stage 3 — Test card shipment
items.text: A 5-card sample kit ships within 3 business days, with Ultralight AES, Ultralight C and Classic 1K variants encoded to the property's VISIONLINE parameters.

items.label: Stage 4 — On-site validation
items.text: Hotel IT or front-desk staff test each sample card on representative Essence, Allure and Classic locks, confirming encoding success, open behavior and encoding persistence.

items.label: Stage 5 — Production approval
items.text: After test results are confirmed, the property approves artwork, quantity, chip selection and encoding schedule for the bulk production run.

faq.question: Should I migrate from MIFARE Classic 1K to Ultralight AES on VingCard locks?
faq.answer: Yes. MIFARE Ultralight AES offers better security, lower manufacturing cost and a smaller memory footprint than Classic 1K. VingCard fully supports Ultralight AES on Essence, Allure and Essence Flex locks with current firmware. The migration requires no lock hardware changes — only new card stock. Most properties can realize 8-12% per-card savings while improving encryption. Properties still using legacy Classic 1K should plan a transition within 12-18 months.

faq.question: What is the difference between MIFARE Ultralight C and Ultralight AES for VingCard?
faq.answer: Both chips have 888 bytes of usable memory, but Ultralight AES adds 128-bit encryption while Ultralight C uses static credentials. For VingCard, Ultralight AES is the recommended path forward because it prevents credential cloning and aligns with VISIONLINE's latest security modules. Ultralight C remains available for properties that prioritize absolute cost minimization, but AES is the better long-term choice.

faq.question: Can VingCard Classic series locks use MIFARE Ultralight AES?
faq.answer: No. The VingCard Classic series supports MIFARE Classic 1K and Ultralight C only. Ultralight AES is only available on Essence, Allure and Essence Flex locks with firmware version 2024 or later. If you need Ultralight AES, you will need to upgrade to an Essence or Allure lock. Properties with existing Classic locks should use Ultralight C as the next upgrade path.

faq.question: How long does Ultralight AES encoding take compared to Classic 1K?
faq.answer: Encoding speed is essentially identical between the two — both take 2-3 seconds per card at the VISIONLINE front-desk encoder. The time difference is negligible, so the decision should be based on security requirements and cost, not encoding speed.

faq.question: Does ProudTek offer pre-encoded VingCard cards?
faq.answer: ProudTek ships cards with the correct chip and antenna configuration but does not pre-encode guest-room credentials. Room-key encoding must happen at the property through VISIONLINE because it requires real-time PMS data such as room number, check-in date and access level. ProudTek can pre-encode common-area access credentials if you provide the VISIONLINE access-group configuration file.

faq.question: Are VingCard-compatible cards affected by the MIFARE Classic vulnerability?
faq.answer: Properties using MIFARE Classic 1K should be aware of known cryptographic weaknesses in the Classic chip family. MIFARE Ultralight C and Ultralight AES do not have the same vulnerabilities. VingCard and ASSA ABLOY recommend properties upgrade to Ultralight C or AES for enhanced security. ProudTek can supply replacement Ultralight cards as a drop-in upgrade.

faq.question: What is the minimum order quantity for VingCard-compatible cards?
faq.answer: Plain white MIFARE Ultralight C or AES cards start at 200 pieces per order. Custom-printed cards with hotel branding require a 500-piece minimum to cover printing setup costs. Test-card kits of 5 pieces are available free for new compatibility projects. Volume pricing at 5,000 and 10,000 pieces offers per-card savings of 12-18%.

faq.question: Do VingCard Essence and Allure locks support mobile credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Both Essence and Allure series support ASSA ABLOY Mobile Access via Bluetooth and NFC for contactless phone-based room entry. This feature must be enabled in your VISIONLINE subscription. Mobile access allows guests to use their smartphones as room keys, reducing physical card demand and improving the guest experience. ProudTek can provide NFC-enabled test cards to validate mobile credential setup during pilot phases.

faq.question: Can I use VingCard-compatible cards with other hotel lock brands?
faq.answer: VingCard-compatible cards are optimized specifically for VingCard lock architecture and VISIONLINE encoding parameters. Using them with non-VingCard locks may result in encoding failures or compatibility issues. Each lock brand uses proprietary encoding schemes, so credentials should always match the installed lock system. ProudTek can help identify compatible cards for other brands if you need multi-system support.
